author: Haffa, Juhani, et al.

This section describes the isolation of tumor cells from ascites fluid collected from ovarian cancer patients.14 This part of the protocol can be adopted for isolating cells from other fluids or tumor entities.CRITICAL: Start this procedure immediately after collection or receipt of the ascites sample.40.Cool down the centrifuge to 4°C.41.Transfer ascites to 50 mL tubes.42.Centrifuge at 800 × g for 10 min at 4°C.Optional: If the ascites volume is very large, ascites can be transferred to larger centrifuge bottles. steps.title: Prepare reagents and casting molds for multi‑well dishes
steps.instruction: Sterilize solutions and molds and pre‑warm culture medium before dish casting.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 9 g NaCl into a dry autoclave‑safe glass bottle, add 1 L sterile water, autoclave, and store the 0.9 % NaCl solution at 20 °C.
Weigh 0.5 g agarose powder into a dry autoclave‑safe glass bottle, loosely screw the lid (no steam entry), autoclave on a dry cycle, and store the agarose powder at 20 °C.
Place casting molds (12‑256 format, 16 × 16 array) in an autoclave‑safe container (e.g., pouches) and autoclave on a dry cycle.
Prepare Culture Medium as described in the Materials section in a sterile hood, pre‑warm at 37 °C, and store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks after use.
Place a sterile 12‑well culture plate on the bench using sterile tweezers or a spatula.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment for tissue sample processing
steps.instruction: Make enzyme aliquots, media, and gather all consumables needed for tumor tissue dissociation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare the Tumor Dissociation Kit enzymes according to the manufacturer’s protocol (Miltenyi link) and aliquot for storage at –20 °C (up to 6 months).
Prepare Stop Medium as described, pre‑warm to 37 °C, and store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Pre‑warm basal DMEM (no additives) to 37 °C.
Pre‑warm Culture Medium to 37 °C.
If cells will be frozen, prepare Freezing Medium as described, pre‑warm an aliquot to 37 °C, and store unused aliquots at –20 °C for up to 1 month.

Gather equipment: pre‑chilled PBS, petri dish, sterile scalpel & tweezers, gentleMACS C Tubes, gentleMACS Dissociator, rotator, 70 µm strainer, 50 mL tubes, ACK Lysis Buffer 1X, Trypan blue solution, cell counter, and (if freezing) labelled cryotubes and a freezing container.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment for ascites sample processing
steps.instruction: Make media and collect consumables needed for ascites cell isolation.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Stop Medium as described, pre‑warm to 37 °C, and store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Pre‑warm Culture Medium to 37 °C.
If cells will be frozen, prepare Freezing Medium as described, pre‑warm an aliquot to 37 °C, and store unused aliquots at –20 °C for up to 1 month.

Gather equipment: 50 mL tubes or larger centrifuge bottles (e.g., Thermo Scientific™ Polypropylene Centrifuge Bottles, Cat No 75‑006‑443) with appropriate inserts, 70 µm strainer, ACK Lysis Buffer 1X, Trypan blue solution, cell counter, and (if freezing) labelled cryotubes and a freezing container.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment for thawing frozen tumor cells
steps.instruction: Warm media and set up heat block for rapid thawing of cryopreserved cells.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm Culture Medium to 37 °C.
Turn on a heat block equipped with a cryotube adapter and set to 37 °C.
Prepare dry ice if frozen cells must be shipped.
Gather 50 mL tubes, Trypan blue solution, and a cell counter.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment for microspheroid recovery and dissociation
steps.instruction: Make recovery medium, pre‑warm enzymes, and collect tools for handling microspheroids.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Recovery Medium as described, pre‑warm to 37 °C, and store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Pre‑warm Culture Medium to 37 °C.
Pre‑warm the required volume of TrypLE™ Express Enzyme 1X to 37 °C.
Turn on a heat block and set to 37 °C.
Gather sterile tweezers or spatula, 2 mL dolphin tubes, a 96‑well flat‑bottom plate (e.g., Sarstedt Cat No 83.3924.005), 20 µm cell strainer, 50 mL tubes, Trypan blue solution, and a cell counter.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment for enrichment of viable cells
steps.instruction: Warm recovery medium and assemble the dead‑cell removal kit.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑warm Recovery Medium to 37 °C.
Gather Dead Cell Removal Kit, LS columns, QuadroMACS™ Separator, sterile double‑distilled water, 15 mL tubes, 2 mL dolphin tubes, and optionally a 20 µm mini‑strainer.

steps.title: Prepare reagents and equipment for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Make flow buffer, set heat block, and collect antibodies and plates for staining.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Flow Buffer as described, keep at 4 °C, and store at 4 °C for up to 1 month.
Turn on a heat block and set to 67 °C.

Gather TruStain FcX, required antibodies (including caspase‑3/7 marker and 7‑AAD), a 96‑well V‑shape microplate (for Attune N×T), 1.5 mL reaction tubes for dead‑cell controls, and start the flow cytometer.

steps.title: Make agarose multi‑well dishes
steps.instruction: Cast, gel, and transfer agarose dishes into a 12‑well plate, then equilibrate with culture medium.

substeps.instruction: Combine 0.5 g autoclaved agarose powder with 25 mL sterile 0.9 % NaCl solution to obtain a 2 % (w/v) agarose solution.
Gently swing the bottle to premix the powder.
Microwave with lid slightly open, checking every 10–15 s, until agarose is fully dissolved (≈1 min). Avoid over‑boiling; the solution will be very hot.
Allow the solution to cool to 60–70 °C (≈5–10 min).
Place casting molds on the bench with indentations facing upward.
Pipette 500 µL of molten agarose into each well of each mold, avoiding bubbles; tap gently to release trapped bubbles. Re‑heat agarose if it has cooled too much.
Let the agarose‑filled molds stand at 20 °C for 20–30 min until gelled.
Invert each mold over a 12‑well plate and flex gently (using sterile tweezers or spatula) to release one agarose dish per well. Handle carefully—agarose dishes break easily (CRITICAL).
Add 2–2.5 mL Culture Medium to each well, incubate ≥15 min, then remove medium surrounding the outside of the dishes.
Repeat the addition of 2–2.5 mL Culture Medium, incubate ≥15 min, and remove surrounding medium again.
Add a final 2–2.5 mL Culture Medium to each well.
Store the plate in a humidified incubator at 37 °C until use. (≈25 mL agarose solution yields ~40 dishes; solution can be reheated for additional batches.)

steps.title: Isolate tumor cells from tissue samples
steps.instruction: Dissociate freshly resected ovarian tumor tissue into a single‑cell suspension using the Miltenyi Tumor Dissociation Kit.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the tissue to a petri dish and wash with pre‑chilled PBS.
Trim away adipose and connective tissue as much as possible.
Mince tissue into 1–5 mm pieces with a sterile disposable scalpel.
Place minced pieces into a gentleMACS C Tube; add 4.7 mL basal DMEM, 200 µL Enzyme H, 100 µL Enzyme R, and 25 µL Enzyme A. Use ≤1 g tissue per tube; split larger samples.
Run gentleMACS program h_tumor_01 followed by h_tumor_02.
Incubate the tube on a rotator at 37 °C, 300 rpm for 1 h.
Run gentleMACS program h_tumor_03.
Filter the suspension through a 70 µm strainer into a 50 mL tube; wash the strainer with 45 mL Stop Medium.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C; discard supernatant.
If the pellet appears red, perform red‑blood‑cell lysis as described in the optional RBC removal section.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL Culture Medium.
Count viable cells using Trypan blue staining.
If cells cannot be used immediately for microspheroid culture, freeze them using the viable cryopreservation protocol (optional).

steps.title: Isolate tumor cells from ascites samples
steps.instruction: Collect and process ascites fluid to obtain a viable single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Cool the centrifuge to 4 °C.
Transfer ascites fluid into 50 mL tubes (or larger centrifuge bottles if volume is high; use appropriate inserts).
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant (store at –80 °C for later use if desired).
Pool all cell pellets; if red, perform RBC lysis as in the optional section.
Resuspend pooled pellet in 10 mL Stop Medium.
Filter through a 70 µm strainer into a 50 mL tube; wash the strainer with up to 40 mL Stop Medium.
Centrifuge at 500 × g for 5 min at 20 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL Culture Medium.
Count viable cells with Trypan blue.
If cells are not used immediately for microspheroid culture, freeze them using the viable cryopreservation protocol (optional).

steps.title: Analyze cell composition by flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Stain single‑cell suspensions from microspheroids with a five‑antibody panel and controls, then acquire data on an Attune NxT cytometer.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 300 × g for 5 min; discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 500 µL Flow Buffer.
Add 5 µL TruStain FcX; mix gently.
Incubate 10 min at 20 °C.

Aliquot 50 µL of the stained suspension into each well of a 96‑well V‑shaped plate (total nine wells): one with all five antibodies, six fluorescence‑minus‑one (FMO) controls (one for each antibody and one for 7‑AAD), one dead‑cell control, and one unstained control.
Prepare 1:50 antibody dilutions in Flow Buffer as per Table 3:
• All five antibodies (CD326, CD45, CD90, PDPN, CD31): 2 µL each antibody + 54 µL Flow Buffer = 60 µL total.
• FMO controls (four antibodies): 1.2 µL each of the four antibodies + 55 µL Flow Buffer = 60 µL.
• FMO control for 7‑AAD (five antibodies): 1.2 µL antibodies + 54 µL Flow Buffer = 60 µL.
Centrifuge plate at 500 × g for 5 min; firmly flip to discard supernatant.
Add 50 µL of the appropriate antibody dilution to each test well; add Flow Buffer alone to dead‑cell and unstained controls.
Mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark.

Add 100 µL Flow Buffer to each well, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min, flip, and resuspend in 100 µL Flow Buffer. Repeat washing (centrifuge, flip, resuspend) two more times for a total of three washes, ending with 100 µL Flow Buffer.
Transfer 50 µL of the dead‑cell control to a 1.5 mL tube and heat at 67 °C for 10 min to generate dead cells; return this suspension to its well.
Add 2 µL 7‑AAD to the five‑antibody sample, all FMO controls (except the 7‑AAD FMO), and the dead‑cell control; mix gently.
Incubate 7 min at 20 °C in the dark.
Resuspend all wells in 150 µL Flow Buffer.
Acquire data on the flow cytometer. (CRITICAL: During washes, cell pellets may be invisible; flip plates firmly but gently to avoid loss.)

steps.title: Cell death assay after drug treatment via flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Stain drug‑treated and control microspheroid cells to assess viability, apoptosis, and cell‑type specific death using 7‑AAD and a caspase‑3/7 detection reagent.

substeps.instruction: Start after step 94 (completion of drug treatment).
Resuspend cells in Flow Buffer:
• Negative/untreated control: 400 µL Flow Buffer.
• Drug‑treated sample: 100 µL Flow Buffer.
If needed, count cells and check for clumps.
Add TruStain FcX (1:100 dilution): 4 µL to negative control, 1 µL to drug‑treated sample; mix gently.
Incubate 10 min at 20 °C.
Transfer the drug‑treated sample to one well of a 96‑well V‑shaped plate.
Divide the negative control into seven 50 µL aliquots and place each into separate wells of the same plate, creating the following seven sample types:
1. All markers (CD326, CD45, 7‑AAD, Caspase‑3/7).
2‑5. Four FMO controls (one for each antibody, one for 7‑AAD, one for Caspase‑3/7).
6. Dead‑cell control.
7. Unstained control.
Prepare 1:50 antibody dilutions in Flow Buffer as per Table 4:
• Sample #1 (all markers, two antibodies): 2 µL each antibody + 57.6 µL Flow Buffer = 60 µL.
• Sample #2 (FMO CD326 with CD45): 1.2 µL each antibody + 58.8 µL Flow Buffer = 60 µL.
• Sample #3 (FMO CD45 with CD326): same as #2.
• Sample #4 (FMO 7‑AAD with two antibodies): 1.2 µL each antibody + 57.6 µL Flow Buffer = 60 µL.
• Sample #5 (FMO Caspase‑3/7 with two antibodies): same as #4.
Centrifuge plate at 500 × g for 5 min; flip to discard supernatant.
Add 50 µL of the appropriate antibody dilution to each test well; add Flow Buffer alone to dead‑cell and unstained controls.
Mix gently by pipetting.
Incubate 20 min at 4 °C in the dark.
Add 100 µL Flow Buffer to each well, centrifuge 500 × g for 5 min, flip, and resuspend in 100 µL Flow Buffer.
Transfer 50 µL of the dead‑cell control to a 1.5 mL tube and heat at 67 °C for 10 min to generate dead cells; return to its well.
Add 0.1 µL CellEvent Caspase‑3/7 green detection reagent to the all‑marker sample and to all FMO controls except the Caspase‑3/7 FMO; mix gently.
Incubate 45 min at 20 °C in the dark.
Add 2 µL 7‑AAD to the all‑marker sample, all FMO controls (except the 7‑AAD FMO), and the dead‑cell control; mix gently.
Incubate 7 min at 20 °C in the dark.
Resuspend all wells in 150 µL Flow Buffer.
Acquire data on the flow cytometer.
